title: Isolar os testes de dispatch do supervisor (implementer e demais fases) do project.toml vivo, no padrao CAM-405, para backend codex ser config commitavel
description: O CAM-405 criou o seam de configPath so para makeReviewDispatch (reviewer). Commitar [backend] implementer = codex quebrou o CI com 85 fails (medido no PR #333, run 30187674682): os testes de runSupervisor (loop.test.ts e familia) leem o project.toml vivo via readPhaseBackend/readPhaseModel sem configPath, entao um tree com backend codex faz o dispatch de teste resolver codex, falhar o auth preflight fail-closed na maquina de CI sem codex auth, e quebrar asserts de spawn-resolution/claude-backed. Fix: estender o seam de configPath (ou injecao equivalente) a TODOS os sites de resolucao de fase consumidos por teste (implementer no loop.ts, planner/auditor no plan-runner, run.ts), com teste de regressao provando que um config codex-resolving nao quebra a suite generica, no mesmo desenho do CAM-405. Desbloqueia: re-aplicar implementer=codex (gpt-5.6-sol) como config commitada; o backend codex ja provou funcionar ao vivo (11/11 stories DONE round-a-round no ciclo CAM-406). Reverter aplicado em ea72a1da deve ser desfeito quando isto shipar.

spec.scope:
Extend the CAM-405 `configPath` injection seam to the three remaining production phase-resolution sites that read the live scripts/cam/project.toml, isolate the generic supervisor and plan-runner test suites onto fixture configs, and then re-commit `[backend] implementer = "codex"` (undoing revert ea72a1da), proven by running the suite under a codex-UNAUTHENTICATED environment.

RE-SPEC NOTE. A first plan attempt escalated after two audit rounds. The auditor confirmed the PRD was accurate and exhaustively verified against the repo, and blocked on ONE defect that originated in this spec, not in the planner: the acceptance oracle was non-falsifiable in the environment where the implementer runs. This re-spec fixes that oracle and folds in the auditor's four secondary findings. The census, seam design and non-goals below were all re-verified by the auditor and are unchanged.

MEASURED CENSUS (verified by two independent read-only sweeps and re-verified by the auditor; do not re-derive). Exactly THREE dispatch sites are un-seamed, which is SIX reader calls, since each site does readPhaseBackend then resolvePhaseModel back-to-back:
  1-2. src/supervisor/loop.ts:1108 readPhaseBackend('implementer') and :1118 resolvePhaseModel({phase:'implementer'}), both inside runSupervisor.
  3-4. src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts:655 readPhaseBackend('planner') and :658 resolvePhaseModel({phase:'planner'}), both inside resolveAndSpawnPlanner.
  5-6. src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts:731 readPhaseBackend('auditor') and :734 resolvePhaseModel({phase:'auditor'}), both inside resolveAndSpawnAuditor.
ALREADY SEAMED, templates and not work: review.ts:394,404 (CAM-405); run.ts:626,627,639 (CAM-425); orch-resolve.ts:74,75,81; config.ts:299,300.

NO signature change is needed anywhere in src/config/: the readers already accept the seam. readPhaseModel(phase, configPath?, backend?) models.ts:158; readPhaseEffort(phase, configPath?) models.ts:197; readBackend(configPath?) models.ts:224; readPhaseBackend(phase, configPath?) models.ts:265; resolvePhaseModel({phase, backend, configPath?, cacheReader?}) model-resolution.ts:145. Each defaults via defaultProjectConfigPath() = join(process.cwd(),'scripts','cam','project.toml') at models.ts:89-91: cwd-relative at call time, no upward search. That is why today's tests must chdir, and why the seam is the correct fix rather than more chdir helpers.

THE MEASURED FAILURE SET (auditor-measured on a throwaway worktree at 787858ac, flip applied, NO seam work). With a codex-authenticated HOME: 5630 pass / 0 fail. With HOME pointed at an empty dir: 5545 pass / 85 fail, exactly reproducing the PR #333 count, concentrated in exactly SEVEN files: test/supervisor/loop.test.ts (74), events (3), ensure-worker-pane (3), test/logging/spawn-resolution (2), pause-halt (1), loop-model-resolution (1), pause-resume (1). The remaining five implementer-side files (implement-blocked-marker-wiring, non-convergence-terminal, notify-orchestrator, test/notify/resend, suggestion-filing-hook) do NOT fail today and are pre-emptive isolation, which is correct to include but carries no live signal. Story splitting should respect that boundary: the seven signal-bearing files are the ones whose isolation is directly falsifiable.

REQUIRED OUTCOMES.
R1. RunSupervisorOptions (src/supervisor/loop.ts:205) gains an optional configPath, threaded to loop.ts:1108 and :1118, documented in the doc-comment style of MakeReviewDispatchOptions.configPath (review.ts:283-299).
R2. RunPlanPhaseOptions (plan-runner.ts:286) gains the same optional configPath, threaded through runPlannerSpawnStep (:1015, invocation :1025) and runAuditorSpawnStep (:1036, invocation :1046) down to the four plan-runner reader calls.
R3. The generic implementer and plan-runner test suites default to a module-level real-tmpdir fixture config declaring the claude backend, in the shape of review.test.ts:268-286 plus :343-350, including the `'configPath' in overrides` opt-out.
R4. One AC5-style codex regression test per newly seamed phase, modelled on review.test.ts:2008, each red-swept.
R5. `implementer = "codex"` re-committed under [backend] in scripts/cam/project.toml, sequenced LAST, and proven under an emptied HOME.

BLAST RADIUS. Implementer: about 168 runSupervisor invocations across 12 files, led by test/supervisor/loop.test.ts (120). Planner and auditor: about 158 plan-phase invocations across 15 files, led by test/supervisor/plan/plan-runner.test.ts (44), plan-runner-replan (31), plan-runner-container (21). Today only about 6 of loop.test.ts's 120 invocations isolate at all, via process.chdir helpers at loop.test.ts:172 and :4251, plan-runner-codex-auth.test.ts:105 and plan-runner-model-resolution.test.ts:124.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: RunSupervisorOptions exposes an optional configPath string field, and both src/supervisor/loop.ts:1108 (readPhaseBackend) and :1118 (resolvePhaseModel) receive it. When configPath is omitted the resolved backend and model are byte-for-byte identical to current behavior. Do NOT introduce a local `??` default at the site: match the review.ts:370-373 pattern where the local is simply the possibly-undefined option.

AC2: RunPlanPhaseOptions exposes the same optional configPath string field, and all four plan-runner reader calls (:655, :658, :731, :734) receive it, threaded from the exported entrypoints runPlanPhase (:1121) and runPlanPhaseWithReplan (:1260) through runPlannerSpawnStep and runAuditorSpawnStep. Omission preserves current behavior byte-for-byte.

AC3: The private helpers resolveAndSpawnPlanner (plan-runner.ts:638) and resolveAndSpawnAuditor (plan-runner.ts:714) currently take 11 positional parameters. Threading may add a parameter or convert them to an options object; growing them to a 12th positional is a legitimate reason to prefer the options object. No call site outside plan-runner.ts changes shape.

AC4: A module-level real-tmpdir fixture config (mkdtempSync, containing at minimum a [backend] section naming claude) is defaulted into the generic implementer test suites via the `'configPath' in overrides ? overrides.configPath : GENERIC_FIXTURE_PATH` idiom, with afterAll cleanup. Existing chdir-based tests opt out with an explicit `configPath: undefined` so they keep covering the live-default path on purpose.
AC5: The same generic-fixture default is applied to the generic plan-runner test suites covering the planner and auditor phases, with the same explicit opt-out.

AC6: Three new codex regression tests, one per newly seamed phase (implementer, planner, auditor). Each stages a tmpdir project.toml selecting the codex backend for that phase plus a [models.codex] pin, injects a faked auth check, and asserts: the auth check was called, the dispatch did not return an error whose detail contains 'codex-auth-failed', and the dispatched command carries the pinned codex model. Modelled on test/supervisor/review.test.ts:2008.

AC7: Each AC6 test is swept red against a tree without its corresponding seam. The durable record of that sweep is an in-file `red-sweep` comment in the new test file (handoff.json rotates per story and must never be an evidence oracle, per scripts/cam/patterns.md:907-909). The implementer must ALSO restate the measured red result in the story's handoff.json summary as free-text, so the literal wording of this criterion is satisfied for a later reviewer, but the in-file comment is the oracle target.

AC8: scripts/cam/project.toml contains `implementer = "codex"` under [backend], restoring what ea72a1da removed. The pre-existing [models.codex] implementer = "gpt-5.6-sol" pin is left untouched. This is the last story in the PRD.

AC9 (ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE, re-oracled): with the AC8 flip applied, the suite must be green under a CODEX-UNAUTHENTICATED environment, i.e. `CAM_AUDIT_HOME=$(mktemp -d) && HOME=$CAM_AUDIT_HOME bun test` (or any equivalent that makes ~/.codex/auth.json unreadable, since codexAuthCheck point-reads join(homedir(),'.codex','auth.json') at src/supervisor/codex-auth.ts:63 with no env-var equivalent). A plain `bun test` on a codex-authenticated machine is EXPLICITLY NOT acceptance evidence: the auditor measured 5630 pass / 0 fail on an unseamed tree with the flip applied, so the plain run is tautological here in exactly the way a green CI on a claude-only config would be. The implementer must record BOTH runs with their pass/fail counts (authenticated and emptied-HOME), so that the localization claim -- that a red result names which file was missed -- is actually true.

AC10 (planner/auditor dress rehearsal): the plan-side isolation must have a falsifiable oracle of its own, not just presence-greps for configPath, since nothing in the committed config ever resolves planner or auditor to codex and so the greps are green on main by construction. Stage a codex-resolving planner/auditor project.toml (or run the plan suites in a throwaway worktree whose live scripts/cam/project.toml selects planner and auditor = codex, under an emptied HOME), record the measured before/after counts, and persist the result in a durable in-file `dress-rehearsal` comment. A cheap additional positive signal: the repo config pins planner = "fable" while DEFAULTS.planner = 'opus' (src/config/models.ts:62-70), so a fixture-resolved planner argv is directly distinguishable from a live-toml-resolved one.

AC11 (comment/runtime drift): every in-file comment asserting the now-false non-injectability contract must be updated to the new fixture-injectable contract. Known occurrences: test/supervisor/loop-model-resolution.test.ts:132-136, test/supervisor/loop.test.ts:539, test/supervisor/loop.test.ts:4246, and test/supervisor/plan/plan-runner-codex-auth.test.ts:19. Oracle: `! grep -rq 'not injectable through RunSupervisorOptions' test/`. Also supersede the CAM-350 US-003 non-injectability note in scripts/cam/patterns.md with a bullet recording the new contract.
AC12: bun run typecheck clean, bun run check:all passing, no new test uses skipIf.
gotchas: THE ORACLE TRAP THAT ESCALATED ROUND 1, do not reintroduce it: the machine that runs this PRD has codex authenticated (/opt/homebrew/bin/codex present; the CAM-406 cycle ran a live codex implementer). Therefore flipping [backend] implementer = codex and running `bun test` is GREEN even with zero seam work: 5630 pass / 0 fail, auditor-measured at 787858ac. The 85 failures only materialize when ~/.codex/auth.json is unreadable, which is the CI condition. Any acceptance criterion for this issue that does not simulate the unauthenticated environment is tautological. See AC9.

codexAuthCheck point-reads join(homedir(), '.codex', 'auth.json') at src/supervisor/codex-auth.ts:63, and its own doc comment at :46 records that there is NO env-var equivalent to Claude Code's config-dir override. Overriding HOME is therefore the available lever (node's homedir() honors HOME on POSIX), not a CODEX_HOME variable.

CORRECTION TO INHERITED CONTEXT: the prior orchestrator handoff and the CAM-425 journal entry both name test/commands/run-configpath-seam.test.ts as the regression-test model. That is WRONG. Its fixture has no [backend] section, so readBackend falls through to DEFAULTS.backend='claude'; its cacheReader is never injected or invoked; it asserts only that a staged model and effort reach the argv. It proves path isolation on a claude-resolving fixture and nothing about codex safety.

The correct model is test/supervisor/review.test.ts, which pairs TWO mechanisms that must BOTH be reproduced. Mechanism (a), the module-level generic fixture at :268-286 defaulted in by makeDispatchOpts at :343-350, is what makes the committed config safe to flip. Mechanism (b), the AC5 codex regression at :2008, is what makes the seam falsifiable. Shipping (b) without (a) leaves CI just as red as today.

NO control-flow reordering is required at any of the three sites, and this must not be re-litigated. Misreading resolve/preflight/build ordering as chronological is what escalated the CAM-398 plan through two audit rounds. The caller's opts object is already in lexical scope at every resolution point: in runSupervisor, opts.codexModelsCacheReaderFn is already read ten lines below the site at :1121; in plan-runner, opts is already destructured at :1021 and :1042.

Both enclosing options interfaces are already dependency-injection-shaped and already carry sibling seams of exactly this kind: codexAuthCheckFn, codexModelsCacheReaderFn, preflightContainerFn, escalateFn. This is an additive field on an established pattern, not a new architecture.

Revert ea72a1da removed only `implementer = "codex"` from [backend] (1 file, 1 deletion) and deliberately KEPT the [models.codex] pin, harmless while no phase resolves to codex because readNestedBackendModel returns undefined when backend is not codex (models.ts:111-125). The same disease was reverted three times on the reviewer phase (04abdb4a, eae0c5f6, e6e46192), which is what motivated CAM-405.

Story-splitting guidance from the auditor: US-003-shaped stories that edit 11-13 test files (~3.5k lines each) are past the 1-3 file heuristic, though the per-file edit is one mechanical ~10-line block. If the runner shows context pressure, split along the MEASURED signal boundary given in the scope: the seven files that actually fail under the flip versus the five pre-emptive ones, and split the plan-side equivalently by directory.

F-02 risk to design against: a test file whose opts builder is bypassed by a direct `runPlanPhase({...})` object literal would still read the live project.toml while a presence-grep oracle stays green. That is why AC10 requires a behavioral dress rehearsal rather than greps alone.

NON-GOAL N1: do NOT thread readPhaseEffort at these three sites. readPhaseEffort is called ONLY from the two orchestrator sites (run.ts:639, orch-resolve.ts:81); implementer, planner and auditor never read [efforts]. Scope creep with no consumer.
NON-GOAL N2: do NOT modify the already-seamed sites (review.ts, run.ts, orch-resolve.ts, config.ts). NON-GOAL N3: do NOT change any signature in src/config/.

OUT OF SCOPE, measured, file separately rather than as a story here: run.ts:584 calls buildOrchestratorBootPrompt() with no argument, and that function (run.ts:225-226) forwards to readMetaLoop(configPath), so the boot prompt's meta-loop read still bypasses the CAM-425 seam. Also out of scope: the stale comment at test/commands/run-model-resolution.test.ts:126 claiming there is no configPath seam.

Naming asymmetry to be aware of, not to fix: the review seam uses readPhaseBackend('reviewer', configPath) while the run seam uses global readBackend(opts.configPath), deliberate per run.ts:610-613. The three sites in scope are per-phase, so they follow the review.ts form.
CI runs `bun run check:all -- --json` per .github/workflows/ci.yml:26, and CI runners are codex-unauthenticated, which is the environment AC9 simulates locally.
domainTerms: configPath seam: an optional configPath field on an already-DI-shaped options interface, threaded to the phase-resolution readers so a test can point resolution at a fixture project.toml instead of the live scripts/cam/project.toml. Introduced by CAM-405 on MakeReviewDispatchOptions, extended by CAM-425 to run.ts.

phase-resolution site: a place in production code where a dispatch resolves the backend and model (and sometimes effort) for one LLM phase, by calling readPhaseBackend/readBackend followed by resolvePhaseModel immediately before building the spawn argv.

generic fixture default: the review.test.ts:343-350 idiom where a test-options builder defaults configPath to a module-level tmpdir fixture, using `'configPath' in overrides` so an explicit undefined is an opt-out rather than a fallback to the default.

tautological oracle: an assertion that passes both with and without the change under test, verifying nothing. Two instances are guarded here: AC7's red-sweep requirement for the seam tests, and AC9's emptied-HOME requirement for the issue-level acceptance evidence.

dress rehearsal: a behavioral run that reproduces the production failure condition locally (here, the codex-unauthenticated environment) so that a test-isolation claim is falsifiable before CI rather than after.

fail-closed auth preflight: codexAuthPreflight refuses to dispatch when the codex backend is selected but no valid ~/.codex/auth.json is readable. Correct in production, and the direct cause of the 85 CI failures when tests resolve codex on an unauthenticated runner.
